hook: The revolutionary who led Vietnam to independence from France.

pages.x: Ho Chi Minh was born Nguyễn Sinh Cung in 1890, in a village in central Vietnam, then a French colony. His father was a scholar of Confucius.
In 1911 he left Vietnam as a kitchen helper on a French ship, and stayed away for 30 years. He worked as a cook in London, it is said under a famous chef, and retouched photographs in Paris.
In 1919, at the peace conference at Versailles, he tried to hand the world leaders a petition asking for rights for the Vietnamese. It was ignored. A year later he became a communist.
He worked for the communist movement in Moscow and China under dozens of false names, and was jailed in Hong Kong.

In 1941 he came home and hid in a cave near the Chinese border, leading a movement to fight Japan and France. On 2 September 1945 in Hanoi he declared independence, quoting the American Declaration: "All men are created equal."
France fought to take back its colony. After eight years of war, his forces crushed the French at Dien Bien Phu in 1954. Vietnam was split in two: a communist North led by Ho, and the South.
In the North his government took land from landlords, and thousands were executed. To many he was "Uncle Ho". He backed the war to take the South, where America sent its troops to fight.

He died in 1969, six years before the North won the war and united the country. Saigon was renamed Ho Chi Minh City. He had asked to be cremated, but his body was embalmed and put on display in Hanoi.
Ho Chi Minh led Vietnam's fight for independence from France and founded communist Vietnam. He is still honoured there as the father of the nation.
pts: Defeated France at Dien Bien Phu
